children.name: text
children: {b:1. Sub-Contractor's General Obligations}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall carry out and complete the Sub-Contract Works and any variations thereto in a good and proper workmanlike manner to the satisfaction of the Contractor, any consultants engaged by the Contractor, and the Contract Administrator in compliance with the terms and conditions of the Sub-Contract and in accordance with the Sub-Contract Documents, the Construction Phase Plan and other Statutory Requirements, using materials and workmanship of the quality and standards therein specified, in co-operation with all others working at the Site, and in conformity with all reasonable instructions, directions and requirements of the Contractor including all reasonable rules of the Contractor for the time being regulating the carrying out of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor shall be deemed to have knowledge of the terms and conditions of the Main Contract (except the detailed prices) and undertakes to observe, perform and comply with all the provisions of the Main Contract on the part of the Contractor so far as they relate and apply to the Sub-Contract Works and are not expressly varied hereunder and the Sub-Contractor acknowledges that any breach by him of this Sub-Contract may cause or contribute to the Contractor breaching its obligations under the Main Contract and becoming liable in damages (including the Main Contract Liquidated Damages) under the Main Contract and all such damages and liquidated damages are hereby agreed to be included as being within the reasonable contemplation of the parties. The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor and shall hold the Contractor harmless against all claims, proceedings, damages, costs and expenses suffered or incurred by it as a result of any breach of this Clause 1.2.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding the provisions of Clause 1.2. and without prejudice to any other remedies the Contractor may have, the Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor against all claims, liabilities, demands, proceedings, damages, costs and expenses made against or incurred by the Contractor in relation to any negligence or breach of duty by the Sub-Contractor or any breach of or failure by him to carry out his obligations under this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall, if not already provided, provide to the Contractor within seven days of executing this Sub-Contract or within seven days of any request to provide the same by the Contractor, the following: -

children.name: text
children: a Parent Company Guarantee and/or Performance Bond if stated as required in, and in the form stated in, the Sub-Contract Particulars;

children.name: text
children: such other collateral warranties as may be required under the Main Contract and as are referred to in the Sub-Contract Particulars duly executed; and

children.name: text
children: the O&M Manuals as may be required under the Main Contract and as are referred to in the Sub-Contract Particulars.

children.name: text
children: It is a condition precedent to any of the obligations of the Contractor under this Sub-Contract (including the Sub-Contractor's right to payment) that the Sub-Contractor shall have duly executed as a Deed and have delivered to the Contractor a signed copy of the Sub-Contract Agreement, and the documents listed in Clauses 1.4.1, 1.4.2 and 1.4.3. No commencement by the Sub-Contractor of the Sub-Contract Works or payment by the Contractor shall constitute any waiver by the Contractor of this condition precedent.

children.name: text
children: In no circumstances whatsoever shall any cutting away alteration or modification of the Sub-Contract Works or the Works be done without the prior written authority of the Contractor and the Sub-Contractor shall be responsible for any damage which is occasioned thereby.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor agrees that it has advised the Contractor of his full requirements with regard to chases, recesses, builderswork and other details ("{b:BWIC}") so that these may be incorporated in the structures as the Sub-Contract Works and the Main Contract Works proceed. Should the Sub-Contractor require any further or alternative BWIC which has not been advised to the Contractor as at the date of this Sub-Contract then the Sub-Contractor shall reimburse the Contractor for any additional costs incurred by the Contractor in respect of such BWIC including but not limited to any costs incurred as a result of such BWIC delaying the Sub-Contract Works and/or the Main Contract Works. For the avoidance of doubt, the Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to an extension to the Completion Date as a result of any additional BWIC notified to the Contractor after the date of this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor agrees to use the project's document management system ("{b:DMS}") where invited to do so to the greatest extent possible. The Sub-Contractor understands that all operational and technical project information will be shared by all parties through the DMS Platform with the exception of payment applications, payment notices and any notices required to be issued under clause 19.1. The Sub-Contractor agrees that they will consult the platform to satisfy themselves of current and up to date project information. The Sub-Contractor agrees to use all DMS tools that are appropriate for the project, including but not limited to Submittals, Daily Logs, Contract Management, RFIs, Design Information, Transmittals, Inspections, Observations, Progress Photographs, Surveys, and Documents.

children.name: text
children: Any information issued via the DMS does not constitute an instruction under Clause 3. Should the Sub-Contractor believe that an instruction is required they should notify the Contractor's Project Quantity Surveyor within 7 days of the date of issue of the information requesting an instruction under Clause 3.

children.name: text
children: {b:2. Design Obligations}

children.name: text
children: The Clause 2 applies only where the Sub-Contract Agreement states that the Sub-Contractor is responsible for the design of all or part of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: Where the Sub-Contractor designs any part of the Sub-Contract Works (including all associated or related works whether permanent or temporary in nature) the Sub-Contractor warrants to the Contractor that he shall exercise all the proper skill and care to be expected of an expertly qualified and competent specialist contractor experienced in carrying out work of a similar scope, nature and size to the Sub-Contract Works in:-

children.name: text
children: the design of the Sub-Contract Works;

children.name: text
children: the selection of kinds and standards of materials and goods for incorporation into the Sub-Contract Works; and

children.name: text
children: the co-ordination and integration of the Sub-Contract's design with the remainder of the Works and design by others.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor further warrants to the Contractor that the Sub-Contract Works shall satisfy any performance specification or other requirements included or referred to in the Sub-Contract and/or Main Contract which relate to the Sub-Contract Works and shall comply with all Statutory Requirements which are applicable to the Sub-Contract Works. If there are any discrepancies or divergences within or between the documents comprising the Sub-Contract Documents and/or the documents comprising the Main Contract (so far as they relate and apply to the Sub-Contract), then the Sub-Contractor shall notify the Contractor of his proposal to deal with such discrepancy or divergence. The Contractor shall decide between the discrepant items or otherwise may accept the Sub-Contractor’s proposal. The Sub-Contractor shall be obliged to comply with the decision or acceptance by the Contractor, without cost to the Contractor and without having any entitlement to an extension of the Sub-Contract Period.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall comply with any requirements in the Main Contract in relation to the submission of any documents and drawings relating to the Sub-Contract Works and shall revise and return any documents and drawings as may be required in accordance with the terms of the Main Contract or as specifically stated in the Sub-Contract Documents. No approval or revision of any documents or drawings by the Contractor or the Employer shall relieve the Sub-Contractor of his obligations and the warranties given under this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor hereby grants to the Contractor a royalty free irrevocable non-exclusive licence to use such documents and drawings prepared and produced by the Sub-Contractor for any purpose relating to the Works and shall allow the Employer licence in similar terms. The licences granted by this clause shall be freely assignable, and shall include a right to sub-let. If required the Sub-Contractor shall supply the Contractor with such drawings, negatives and information showing or describing the Sub-Contract Works as built and concerning the maintenance, operation and management of the Sub-Contract Works as may be required under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor may be required to use a document management system  on the project if invited to do so to by the Contractor. This DMS will be used, in conjunction with other methods, of disseminating project design information to the Sub-Contractor. It will be the Sub-Contractor’s responsibility to review, weekly until practical completion of the Works and/or when notified by the DMS of any new content, any and all documentation uploaded to the DMS and to incorporate the same information into the Sub-Contract works. .  The Sub-Contractor will be liable for any costs and or delay incurred by the Contractor or Others for any failure of the Sub-Contractor to take into account the information contained in the DMS as set out in this clause.

children: {b:3. Instructions and Variations}

children.name: text
children: All instructions issued by the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor under either this Clause 3.1, Clause 3.2, Clause 3.3 or Clause 3.4 in respect of the Sub-Contract Works, shall be of no effect unless issued or confirmed in writing by the Contractor's Project Quantity Surveyor or a Director. The Sub-Contractor shall comply with all such instructions forthwith. If after issue of a written notice by the Contractor requiring compliance with an instruction the Sub-Contractor does not so comply within the period specified within the notice (or if no period is specified then within seven days) then the Contractor may employ and pay other persons to execute any work which may be necessary to give effect to such instruction. All costs and expenses incurred by the Contractor in connection with such employment shall be recoverable from the Sub-Contractor as a debt.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor may, by means of a written instruction to the Sub-Contractor, alter or modify the design, quantity or quality of, or the conditions under which the Sub-Contract Works shall be executed, and such alterations or modifications shall not vitiate this Sub-Contract. Unless any such alterations modifications variations or changes are due to the Sub-Contractor's negligence, omission or default, such alterations modifications variations or changes shall be valued and paid for by the Contractor at the prices contained in the Sub-Contract Documents or where the varied or altered work differs from that originally tendered for, at prices or charges analogous thereto, or in the absence of such prices in the Sub-Contract Documents, at a fair and reasonable rate determined by the Contractor, at a fair and reasonable rate determined by the Contractor to be determined at a later date or if applicable, in accordance with Clause 3.5 or Clause 3.6.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor may, by means of a written instruction to the Sub-Contractor, omit any part of or all of the Sub-Contract Works at any time. Such omission shall result in a reduction in the Sub-Contract Price, to be valued in accordance with the Sub-Contract Documents at a fair and reasonable rate determined by the Contractor. The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to recover any loss of profit, overheads or other costs in respect of an omission of any part of or all of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall issue instructions in regard to the expenditure of any defined provisional sums referred to in the Sub-Contract Documents. Within 7 days of the date of execution of this Sub-Contract the Sub-Contractor shall confirm to the Contractor the notice period which the Sub-Contractor requires for the instruction of each defined provisional sum. The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to an extension of time and/or additional cost or loss and/or expense in respect of the expenditure of the defined provisional sums if:

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor receives instruction from the Contractor to expend such defined provisional sum within the notice period confirmed by the Sub-Contractor pursuant to this Clause 3.4; or

children.name: text
children: the Sub-Contractor fails to confirm to the Contractor a notice period for the provisional sum in accordance with this Clause 3.4.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor may not claim payment for daywork unless the Sub-Contractor has given to the Contractor reasonable prior written notice of any work pursuant to any variation or change as referred to in Clause 3.2 above for which he intends to apply for payment on a daywork basis and the Contractor has agreed that such work is to be carried out on a daywork basis. The Sub-Contractor shall deliver to the Contractor by the day of the week stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars signed daywork sheets in the form required by the Contractor giving full details of labour, materials and plant.

children.name: text
children: Where work is agreed by the Contractor to be carried out on a daywork basis payment for such work will be made in accordance with the "Definition of Prime Cost of Daywork carried out under a Building Contract" issued by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors ({b:RICS}) and the Construction Confederation as current at the Base Date together with Percentage Additions to each section of the prime cost at the rates stated in the document identified in the Sub-Contract Particulars or, if they apply in respect of labour, at the All-Inclusive Rates stated in such document or where the work is within the province of any specialist trade and the RICS and the appropriate body representing the employers in that trade have agreed and issued a definition of prime cost of daywork, the prime cost of such work calculated in accordance with that definition current at the Base Date, together with Percentage Additions on the prime cost at the rates stated in the document identified in the Sub-Contract Particulars or, if they apply in respect of labour, at the All-Inclusive Rates stated in such document.

children.name: text
children: {b:4. Commencement and Completion}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall commence the Sub-Contract Works on the Planned Sub-Contract Start Date unless the Sub-Contractor has received written notice from the Contractor that the Sub-Contract Start Date is to be deferred in accordance with this Clause 4.1. The Contractor may defer the Sub-Contract Start Date by up to 3 calendar months from the date stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars. The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to additional cost or loss and/or expense in respect of a deferment to the Sub-Contract Start Date in accordance with this Clause 4.1.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall regularly and diligently carry out the Sub-Contract Works (including the production of and the obtaining of all necessary approvals of any drawings, details or calculations for which he is responsible) at such times and such periods as will suit the progress of the Main Contract
Works and as may be directed by the Contractor and shall complete the Sub-Contract Works or any sections thereof within the Sub-Contract Period(s) as may be amended in accordance with Clause 4.3.

children.name: text
children: If it becomes apparent that the Sub-Contract Works will not be completed by the Completion Date then the Sub-Contractor shall provide written notification to the Contractor setting out the material circumstances as to the cause or causes of the delay including specifying the Relevant Sub-Contract Event that the Sub-Contractor considers has caused the delay and the period of time that the Sub-Contract Works has been delayed by as a consequence. Subject to receiving such notification in accordance with this Clause 4.3 the Contractor shall grant to the Sub-Contractor such extension of time as is reasonable for completion of the Sub-Contract Works to the extent that delay has been caused to the Sub-Contract Works by reason of a Relevant Sub-Contract Event and completion of the Sub-Contract Works will be delayed beyond the Completion Date.

children.name: text
children: It shall be a strict condition precedent to the Sub-Contractor's entitlement to an extension of time that the Sub-Contractor has notified the Contractor under Clause 4.3 within the Notice Period of the date when it becomes or ought to have become, reasonably apparent to the Sub-Contractor that the commencement, progress or completion of the Sub-Contractor Works is being or is likely to be delayed.

children.name: text
children: Whether or not an extension of time is given under Clause 4.3, the Contractor shall notify the Sub-Contractor of his decision as soon as is reasonably practicable.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall constantly use his best endeavours to prevent delay in the progress of the Sub-Contract Works, however caused, and to prevent their completion being delayed or further delayed beyond the Completion Date.

children.name: text
children: In the event of any delay the Sub-Contractor shall do all that may reasonably be required to the satisfaction of the Contractor to proceed with the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to an extension of time where the delay caused by the Relevant Sub-Contract Event is concurrent with one or more delays for which the Sub-Contractor is responsible.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall:

children.name: text
children: Notify the Contractor, no later than the date stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars, of the date when in his opinion, the Sub-Contactor believes that the Sub-Contract Works as a whole will be practically complete.

children.name: text
children: Provide with the notification under 4.9.1, if he has not done so already, the information set out in Clause 1.4 above. the Sub-Contract Works will not have reached practical completion.

children.name: text
children: On receipt of such notification and information under Clause 4.9, the Contractor shall inspect the Sub-Contract Works as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than the date of Sub-Contractor's anticipated practical completion date.

children.name: text
children: Where following the inspection under Clause 4.10 the Contractor agrees that the Sub-Contract Works are completed, the Contractor shall issue a statement of Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works and Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works shall be deemed for all purposes of this Sub-Contractor to have taken place on the date stated in that statement.

children.name: text
children: If the Contractor does not agree that the Sub-Contract Works are completed, it shall notify the Sub-Contractor of the work it requires to be completed before Practical Completion will occur and the

Sub-Contractor shall carry out such works as instructed. When the Contractor is satisfied that such work has been completed by the Sub-Contractor, it shall notify the Sub-Contractor in accordance with Clause 4.11.

children.name: text
children: For the avoidance of doubt, the date of Practical Completion under Clause 4.11 or 4.12 shall in any event be no later than the date of practical completion of the Main Contract Works under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor is in delay in carrying out the Sub-Contract Works and/or fails to complete the Sub-Contract Works in a reasonable and diligent manner on or before the relevant period for completion, the Sub-Contractor shall pay or allow to the Contractor the amount of any loss and/or expense suffered or incurred by the Contractor that is caused by such delay and/or failure.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contract Works are not completed by the Completion Date or any later date fixed under Clause 4.3, the Sub-Contractor shall pay or allow to be paid to the Contractor liquidated and ascertained damages at the rate stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars as between the Completion Date (as extended under Clause 4.3 if applicable) and the date when Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works occurs.

children.name: text
children: {b:5. Vesting of Property and Risk in the Sub-Contract}

children.name: text
children: All equipment materials and goods not for incorporation in the Sub-Contract Works brought on to the site by the Sub-Contractor shall be at the sole risk of the Sub-Contractor. All equipment, materials and goods on the Site for incorporation in the Sub-Contract Works shall become the property of and vest in the Contractor upon delivery but the Sub-Contractor shall be solely responsible for any damage to them and shall remain liable for their safe keeping. The Sub-Contractor shall ensure that such equipment, materials and goods shall not be removed from the Site unless the Contractor so instructs or permits.

children.name: text
children: Risk in the Sub-Contract Works and each part thereof shall remain with the Sub-Contractor until completion of the Sub-Contract Works or the Contractor shall specifically agree in writing to the contrary. The Sub-Contractor shall protect the Sub-Contract Works and each part thereof and all or any part or parts of the Main Contract Works which may in any way be affected by the carrying out of the Sub-Contract Works or otherwise until completion of the Sub-Contract Works as may be directed by the Contractor without addition to the Sub-Contract Sum.

children.name: text
children: {b:6. Indemnity and Insurance}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall be liable for and shall indemnify the Contractor against the matters which the Contractor undertakes to indemnify the Employer under the Main Contract insofar as such matters relate to the Sub-Contract Works. Without prejudice to the obligation to so indemnify the Sub-Contractor shall take out and maintain the necessary insurance against Employer's Liability and third-party liability risks for not less than the sums set out in the Sub-Contract Particulars. The Sub-Contractor shall produce documentary evidence to the Contractor if such insurance ceases to be available so that the parties can discuss the best means of protecting their respective interests.

children.name: text
children: If required, and subject to Clause 6.6, the Sub-Contractor shall take out or maintain professional indemnity insurance for a period of 12 years from practical completion of the Main Contract Works for the amount set out in the Sub-Contract Particulars in respect of any negligence by the Sub-Contractor in the design of any works, goods and/or materials provided that the same is available at commercially reasonable terms. The Sub-Contractor shall inform the Contractor if such insurance ceases to be available so that the parties can discuss the best means of protecting their respective interests.

children.name: text
children: Whenever reasonably requested by the Contractor the Sub-Contractor shall produce as soon as reasonably practicable for inspection evidence that such policies of insurance referred to in Clauses 6.1 and 6.2 are being maintained. If the Sub-Contractor shall fail to take out or maintain the insurance required in Clauses 6.1 and 6.2 then the Contractor may, without prejudice to any other rights or remedies it possesses, take out or maintain the insurances and the costs thereof including any premiums payable shall be recoverable from the Sub-Contractor as a debt.

children.name: text
children: The plant, equipment, materials or other property belonging to the Sub-Contractor (other than materials or goods on Site for use in the Sub-Contract Works) shall be at the sole risk of the Sub-Contractor and any loss or damage to the same, or caused by the same, shall be the sole liability of the Sub-Contractor who shall indemnify the Contractor against any loss, claims or proceedings arising therefrom. The Sub-Contractor will insure any plant, equipment or materials owned by, hired and/or loaned to the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall take out and maintain or procure that the Employer takes out and maintains the insurance of the Works in accordance with the Main Contract and shall procure that either the Sub-Contractor is recognised as a joint name insured or that the insurers waive any rights of subrogation against the Sub-Contractor. The cover afforded to the Sub-Contractor in relation to the Sub-Contract Works will be limited to those perils as set out in the Main Contract and the Sub-Contractor shall observe and comply with the conditions contained in the Contractor's or Employer's insurance policy relating to the Works and shall (if required) pay the excesses due if any claim arises due to the negligence, omission or default of the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children: Where Clause 22.2 applies, the Sub-Contractor shall take out or maintain professional indemnity insurance for a period of 15 years from practical completion of the Main Contract Works in the same terms as otherwise required under clause 6.2.

children.name: text
children: {b:7. Provision of Facilities}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall provide everything necessary for the proper execution and completion of the Sub-Contract Works, except where expressly excluded in the Sub-Contract Particulars, but shall have the use of water, temporary lighting and if and when erected, standing scaffolding (however the Contractor does not guarantee that scaffolding will be available at the time and/or location requested by the Sub-Contractor). The Contractor reserves the right to supply electricity at 110volts. All facilities supplied by the Contractor shall be used under the express condition that no warranty or liability on the part of the Contractor or any other sub-contractors shall be implied or created with regard to the fitness, condition of suitability of such facilities.

children.name: text
children: {b:8. Payment}

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall notify to the Sub-Contractor the name and contact details of the individual to whom each application for interim payment ("{b:Payment Application}") should be submitted. The Sub-Contractor shall submit to the individual notified by the Contractor and to accounts@culenalondon.co.uk a Payment Application on the dates stated in the Payment Schedule. In the event that no such dates are so stated in the Payment Schedule then each Payment Application shall be submitted in the manner set out above no later than 14 calendar days before the date on which each interim payment becomes due. Payment Applications must utilise the format appended to this Sub-Contract and shall include:

children.name: text
children: a brief description of the Sub-Contract Works;

children.name: text
children: a brief, but clear description of each element of the works properly executed in accordance with this Sub-Contract and for any unfixed equipment, materials and goods properly stored on the Site for incorporation in the Works;

children.name: text
children: a statement of the sum that the Sub-Contractor considers will become due on the payment due date in respect of the interim payment, to include the Sub-Contractor's valuation of each element of the works and equipment, materials and goods described in Clause 8.1.2 above;

children.name: text
children: the basis on which such sum has been calculated together with supporting documentation evidencing the carrying out of such works and/or delivery of such equipment, materials and goods; and

children.name: text
children: such other documents or information as the Contractor may reasonably require.

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clause 8.5, the first interim payment to the Sub-Contractor shall be due on the date stated in the Payment Schedule. In the event that no such date is so stated in the Payment Schedule or in the event that no such Payment Schedule is annexed to this Sub-Contract, then the first interim payment to the Sub-Contractor shall be due 45 days after the final Business Day of the month in which the Sub-Contract Works commenced on the Site.

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clause 8.5, interim payments to the Sub-Contractor shall thereafter be due on the dates stated in the Payment Schedule. In the event that no such dates are so stated in the Payment Schedule or in the event that no such Payment Schedule is annexed to this Sub-Contract, then interim payments shall thereafter be due on the same date in each month as that on which the first payment became due save that where the first interim payment becomes due on a date which does not recur in the subsequent month, the interim payment for that subsequent month shall be due on the final Business Day of that month.

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clause 8.5, the final date for payment of each interim payment shall be the date stated in the Payment Schedule. In the event that no such date is so stated in the Payment Schedule or in the event that no such Payment Schedule is annexed to this Sub-Contract, then the final date for payment of each interim payment shall be the later of:

children.name: text
children: 45 calendar days after the date on which it becomes due; or

children.name: text
children: 45 calendar days after the date of receipt by the Contractor from the Sub-Contractor of any required VAT invoice for the amount stated as due in the notice given under Clause 8.7.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to any other rights and remedies available to the Contractor under this Sub-Contract, the Sub-Contractor acknowledges and agrees that the submission of a valid Payment Application is and shall be a condition precedent to that interim payment becoming due and to the Sub-Contractor's entitlement to that interim payment. If the Sub-Contractor fails to submit or is late in submitting its Payment Application or the Sub-Contractor's Payment Application is not properly particularised or substantiated in accordance with Clause 8.1 then the Sub-Contractor's Payment Application may not be processed that month and the Sub-Contractor's entitlement to an interim payment in respect of the amount claimed may be deferred until the following month or the month following the submission of a properly particularised and substantiated Payment Application.

children.name: text
children: The amount due for each interim payment shall be the Contractor's gross valuation determined in accordance with the Sub-Contract Documents less any amounts which may be deducted as Retention and trade discount as specified in the Sub-Contract Particulars and less the total amount due in previous interim payments in respect of the Sub-Contract Works and less any other amounts that the Contractor is entitled to withhold, deduct or set-off pursuant to the terms of this Sub-Contract or otherwise arising out of or in connection with this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall no later than five (5) days after the date on which an interim payment becomes due to the Sub-Contractor give a written notice to the Sub-Contractor which shall specify the sum that the Contractor considers to be or to have been due at the payment due date and the basis on which that sum is calculated (a "{b:Payment Notice}"). It is immaterial that the sum considered to be due may be zero or a negative sum. Subject to any Pay Less Notice given to the Sub-Contractor under Clause 8.8, the sum to be paid by the Contractor shall be the sum specified in the Payment Notice. If the Contractor fails to give a Payment Notice in accordance with this Clause 8.7, the sum to be paid by the Contractor shall, subject to any Pay Less Notice given under Clause 8.8, be the sum specified in the Payment Application.

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clause 8.7 and the remainder of this Clause 8.8 and in addition to the Contractor's common law right of set-off, the Contractor may deduct from any sums due or to become due to the Sub-Contractor under this Sub-Contract, the amount of any claim and/or counterclaim for damages, losses, demands, expenses (including reasonable legal and other professional expenses), costs, liabilities and/or fines which the Contractor may have against the Sub-Contractor under or arising out of this Sub-Contract or any other sub-contract between the Contractor and the Sub-Contractor. The foregoing entitlement is in addition to and not in substitution for any other rights of counterclaim, set-off or abatement available to the Contractor. If the Contractor intends to pay less than the sum stated as due from him in the Payment Notice or Payment Application (as the case may be), the Contractor shall give written notice (a "{b:Pay Less Notice}") of this intention to the Sub-Contractor. The Pay Less Notice shall specify the sum that the Contractor considers to be due to the Sub-Contractor as at the final date for payment of such sum pursuant to Clause 8.4 and the basis on which that sum is calculated. It is immaterial that the sum considered to be due may be zero or a negative sum. The Contractor shall issue such Pay Less Notice no later than the date stated in the Payment Schedule. In the event that no such date is so stated in the Payment Schedule or in the event that no such Payment Schedule is annexed to this Sub-Contract, such Pay Less Notice shall be given by the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor no later than one (1) calendar day before the final date for payment pursuant to Clause 8.4.

children.name: text
children: In the event that the Sub-Contract Works or any part thereof are not completed within the Sub-Contract Period(s) and the Contractor is required to make payment to the Sub-Contractor during such extended period, the Payment Schedule shall (if it is specific to the Sub-Contract Period(s)) be deemed to apply {i:mutatis mutandis} on the same intervals and time periods as set out in the Payment Schedule, from the last dates which appear in the Payment Schedule to the extended period and all payments shall be made in accordance with the extended Payment Schedule.

children.name: text
children: The Retention which may be deducted and retained by the Contractor shall be calculated as follows:

children.name: text
children: where the Sub-Contract Works or any section thereof have not reached Practical Completion in accordance with Clause 4.11, the Retention which the Contractor may deduct and retain as referred to in Clause 8.6 shall be the percentage stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars;

children.name: text
children: The percentage of the Retention stated in the Sub-Contract Particulars shall be released upon the date stated in the Payment Schedule provided that Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works has been achieved by such date. If no date is so stated in the Payment Schedule or if no Payment Schedule is annexed to this Sub-Contract the date for release of the above percentage of the Retention shall be 3 months after Practical Completion of the Main Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: Subject to Practical Completion of the Sub-Contract Works having been achieved and there being no defects, shrinkages or other faults of the types referred to in Clause 15 apparent at a date which is 18 months after the final date for payment of the portion of the Retention calculated in accordance with Clause 8.10.2 herein (the "{b:Retention Release Date}") any balance of the Retention shall be included in the next interim payment due. If those preconditions are not then satisfied, the balance shall be included in the payment next following such completion and the making good of any apparent defects. If not already notified to the Sub-Contractor, any apparent defects shall be listed and notified to him within 14 days of the Retention Release Date.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor Shall write to the Contractor applying for any balance of Retention within 3 months of it falling due in accordance with clause 8.10.3. In the event that the Sub-Contractor fails to write to the Contractor then the Sub-Contractor shall have rescinded any rights to the monies held in accordance with Clause 8.10.1 to 8.10.3.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor's employment is determined under Clause 16.1, 16.2, 16.3 or 16.3A no further sum shall become due to the Sub-Contractor under this Sub-Contract other than any amount that may become due to him under Clause 16.4 and the Contractor need not pay any sum that has already become due either:

children.name: text
children: insofar as the Contractor has given or gives a Pay Less Notice under Clause 8.8; or

children.name: text
children: if the Sub-Contractor, after the last date upon which such Pay Less Notice could have been given by the Contractor in respect of that sum, has become insolvent within the meaning of section 113 of the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996.

children.name: text
children: In the event of the Contractor failing to pay any sum due to the Sub-Contractor by the final date for payment, the Contractor shall pay to the Sub-Contractor interest on such overdue sum from the final date for payment until payment is made at the rate of 3% per annum above the official dealing rate of the Bank of England current at the final date for payment.

children.name: text
children: If the Contractor fails to pay the Sub-Contractor in accordance with Clauses 8.6 to 8.8 by the final date for payment, and the failure continues for 7 days after the Sub-Contractor has given notice to the Contractor of his intention to suspend the performance of his obligations under this Sub-Contract and the ground or grounds on which it is intended to suspend performance, the Sub-Contractor may suspend performance of any or all of his obligations until payment is made in full. Where the Sub-Contractor exercises his right of suspension under this Clause 8.13, he shall be entitled to a reasonable amount in respect of costs and expenses reasonably incurred by him as a result of this exercise of such right.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contract Sum is exclusive of VAT and any payment to the Sub-Contractor under this Sub-Contract shall be net of VAT. The Contractor shall pay the amount of any VAT properly chargeable to Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs as is required under Legislation and VAT notices at the time of the payment. It is a condition precedent to the Sub-Contractor receiving payment under the Sub-Contract that the Sub-Contractor agrees to the adoption by the Contractor of the self-billing procedures for Value Added Tax purposes.

children.name: text
children: The obligation of the Contractor to make any payment under this Sub-Contract is subject to the provisions of the Construction Industry Scheme under the Finance Act 2004 or any subsequent revisions thereof.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contract Sum is fixed for the duration of the Works.

children.name: text
children: The Final Sub-Contract Sum shall be the Sub-Contract Sum as may be adjusted under Clause 3 or any other term of this Sub-Contract and less any other amounts that the Contractor is entitled to withhold, deduct or set-off pursuant to the terms of this Sub-Contract or otherwise arising out of or in connection with this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: Not later than 2 months after completion of the Sub-Contract Works the Sub-Contractor shall send to the Contractor its final account application including all documents necessary for calculating the Final Sub-Contract Sum. Without prejudice to any other rights and remedies available to the Contractor under this Sub-Contract and subject to Clause 8.21 and Clause 8.22, the Sub-Contractor acknowledges and agrees that the submission of a valid final account application in accordance with this Clause is a condition precedent to the Final Payment (calculated in accordance with Clause 8.24) becoming due and to the Sub-Contractor's entitlement to that Final Payment.

children.name: text
children: Not later than 8 months after receipt by the Contractor of the documents referred to in Clause 8.18, the Contractor shall prepare and send to the Sub-Contractor a statement of the calculation of the Final Sub-Contract Sum.

children.name: text
children: If the Contractor does not receive the documents referred to in Clause 8.18 from the Sub-Contractor within 2 months of Completion of the Sub-Contract Works, the Contractor shall prepare a statement of all adjustments to the Sub-Contract Sum as the Contractor is able to make on the information in his possession and the Contractor shall send a copy of such statement to the Sub-Contractor ("{b:the Contractor's Final Statement}").

children.name: text
children: If nothing in the Contractor's Final Statement is disputed in writing by the Sub-Contractor, giving grounds for so disputing, within 1 month of the submission of the Contractor's Final Statement to the Sub-Contractor in accordance with Clause 8.19, the statement of the calculation of the Final Sub-Contract Sum contained within the Contractor's Final Statement shall be deemed to have taken into account all adjustments required by these conditions.

children.name: text
children: The due date for the Final Payment shall be 2 months after whichever of the following occurs last:

children.name: text
children: the Retention Release Date;

children.name: text
children: the date of issue of the Contractor's statement under Clause 8.19; or

children.name: text
children: the date of issue of the Contractor's Final Statement under Clause 8.20.

children.name: text
children: Not later than 5 days after the due date, the Contractor shall send the final Payment Notice to the Sub-Contractor. The Final Payment Notice shall show the Final Sub-Contract Sum, calculated in accordance with Clause 8.18, less the total amount previously due as interim payments under this Sub-Contract and the Final Payment shall be the difference (if any) between the two sums. The difference shall be shown in the Final Payment Notice as a balance due from the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor or from the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor, as the case may be, and the Final Payment Notice shall state the basis on which that amount has been calculated.

children.name: text
children: The final date for payment of the Final Payment shall be 28 days from its due date.

children.name: text
children: If the Party by whom the Final Payment is stated to be payable ("the {b:Payer}") intends to pay less than the stated balance, he shall not later than 5 days before the final date for payment give the other Party a Pay Less Notice in accordance with Clause 8.8.

children.name: text
children: Where a Pay Less Notice is given, the payment to be made on or before the final date for payment shall not be less than the amount stated as due in the notice.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to any of the Contractor's entitlement to deduct and/or withhold monies from the Sub-Contractor in relation to an interim payment or the Final Payment (in accordance with the provisions of Clause 8) the Contractor is also entitled to set off from any interim payment and/or from the Final Payment, an amount in respect of Sub-Contactor Liquidated Damages in accordance with Clause 8.29 and/or any amount due to the Contractor from the Sub-Contractor howsoever arising, including, but not limited to, the Contractor's estimate of an amount due from the Sub-Contractor whether or not such claim has been made at the date of set-off, and the amounts due under other contracts between the Contractor and the Sub-Contractor even to the extent that such contracts relate to a different project.

children.name: text
children: Nothing contained in this Sub-Contract (other than to the giving of notices) shall remove or limit any right of the Contractor under any statute or rule of law or equity in the nature of set-off or abatement of price.

children.name: text
children: the Contractor may at any time (subject to the requirement to issues notices) set-off any liability of the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor against any liability of the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor whether either liability is present or future, liquidated or unliquidated, and whether or not either liability arises under this Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: Any exercise by the Contractor of its rights under this clause shall not limit or affect any other rights or remedies available to it under this Sub-Contract or otherwise.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to the Contractor's rights to claim direct loss and expense pursuant to the provisions of Clause 8.8 the Sub-Contractor shall, subject to the provisions of this Clause 8.29 be liable for the Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages and shall pay to the Contractor and/or the Contractor shall be entitled to withhold or deduct the Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages (at a rate as set out in the Sub-Contract Particulars and/or the Sub-Contract Agreement) in the event of the Sub-Contractor's late completion of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor acknowledges and agrees that the Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages represent the minimum loss and expense that will be incurred by the Contractor in the event that the Sub-Contractor fails to complete the Sub-Contract Works or such works in any Section within the relevant period or periods for completion.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor's liability to pay Main Contract Liquidated Damages or otherwise shall not affect the Contractor's entitlement to recover or the Sub-Contractor's liability to pay the Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages.

children.name: text
children: For the purposes of this Clause 8.29 the Parties agree and acknowledge that:

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages are a genuine pre-estimate, assessed on or before the date of this Sub-Contract of the Contractor's minimum losses and does not take into consideration any liability on the part of the Contractor to pay or allow the Main Contract Liquidated Damages arising out of the late completion of the Sub-Contract Works;

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contract Liquidated Damages are distinct and entirely separate from the Main Contract Liquidated Damages and the Sub-Contractor has discussed, debated and fully agreed this Clause 8.29 and is fully aware of the amount of the Main Contract Liquidated Damages.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Sub-Contract, in the event that the Employer or any other party responsible for making payments under or in connection with the Main Contract is or becomes insolvent the Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to be paid any further sums under or arising out of this Sub-Contract, except to the extent that the Contractor actually receives or recovers any monies from the Employer or any other party responsible for making payments under or in connection with the Main Contract or any liquidator, administrator or receiver which include an amount that is specifically attributable to the Sub-Contract Works. For the purposes of this Clause 8.13.4, "insolvent" shall have the meaning given to that expression by section 113 of the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 and/or as defined under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: If in the execution of this Sub-Contract the Sub-Contractor incurs any direct loss and/or expense because the regular progress of the Sub-Contract Works or of any part of them has been materially affected by any Relevant Sub-Contract Event, the Sub-Contractor shall, subject to clause 4:3 and compliance with the provisions of clause 4:4, be entitled to reimbursement of the actual demonstrable daily costs capped at £150.00 per working day, as a direct result of the Relevant Sub-Contract Event. These incurred costs shall be verified by production of demonstrable evidence of cost in the form of invoices and bank statements. The amount payable by the Contractor under this clause 8.31 shall be the sole entitlement of the Sub-Contractor in respect of the events and circumstances giving rise to any delay in respect of which the extra costs are payable and such amount is accepted by the Sub-Contractor in full and final satisfaction of all claims, demands, actions, suits or proceedings which the Sub-Contractor may make against the Contractor in respect of delay.

children.name: text
children: {b:9. Supervision}

children.name: text
children: At all times during the carrying out of the Sub-Contract Works the Sub-Contractor shall provide all necessary supervision to ensure the proper execution of the Sub-Contract Works and shall have a competent person in charge on the Site who shall be authorised to accept instructions and directions on behalf of the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children: {b:10. Access and Use of Site and Work of others}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall have access to such part or parts of the Site as the Contractor may direct. The Sub-Contractor acknowledges that such access shall be in common with other sub-contractors and suppliers and the Sub-Contractor shall not impede such other sub-contractors and suppliers in the execution of their work on the Site.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall satisfy himself before commencing the Sub-Contract Works as to the work previously carried out by others which may affect the Sub-Contract Works and shall immediately notify the Contractor in writing of any difficulties with the same. Failure to notify the Contractor of any such difficulties may involve the Sub-Contractor in abortive work which shall be made good at no cost to the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor and the Contract Administrator shall at all times have access to the Sub-Contract Works and to any workshop or other place where any equipment materials or goods are being prepared for incorporation in the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: {b:11. Statutory Obligations and Health and Safety}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall comply at no cost to the Contractor with:

children.name: text
children: all health and safety legislation relevant to the Sub-Contract Works and the manner in which they are being carried out;

children.name: text
children: all reasonable directions of the Contractor to the extent necessary for compliance by the Contractor and the Sub-Contractor with such legislation as it affects the Sub-Contract Works; and

children.name: text
children: within the time reasonably required, any written request by the Contractor for information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance by the Sub-Contractor with this Clause 11.1.

children.name: text
children: the requirements of the Bribery Act 2010 and shall take all reasonable endeavours to prevent any infringement of the Bribery Act 2010 within its own organisation or any of its associated organisations.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to the Sub-Contractor's obligations under Clause 11.1, the Sub-Contractor shall comply at no cost to the Contractor with:

children.name: text
children: all of the Contractor's health and safety, quality assurance and environmental policies and procedures, copies of which are available from the Contractor's site office, and the Sub-Contractor shall immediately inform the Contractor if any of such policies and procedures conflict with the requirements of any legislation which will prevail over such policies and procedures if there is any conflict; and

children.name: text
children: all reasonable requirements of the Contractor to the extent that such requirements are necessary for compliance by the Contractor with his obligations under all United Kingdom health and safety and environmental legislation or obligations under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall, prior to commencement of the Sub-Contract Works and at any time thereafter upon request, submit to the Contractor a written statement of the Sub-Contractor, a general policy and method of his specific policy for the Sub-Contract Works in relation to health, safety and welfare, including the appointment of a suitable person responsible for the safe execution of the Sub-Contract Works.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding the generality of the foregoing the Sub-Contractor undertakes to comply with the CDM Regulations and shall:

children.name: text
children: provide the Contractor with any information which the Contractor considers is or may be necessary to ensure that the Construction Phase Plan continues to comply with the CDM Regulations;

children.name: text
children: comply at no cost to the Employer or Contractor with all reasonable requirements of the Contractor relating to compliance by the Sub-Contractor with the CDM Regulations, and no extension of time shall be given in respect of such compliance; and

children.name: text
children: within the time reasonably required in writing by the Contractor, provide to the Contractor such information in respect of the Sub-Contract Works as is reasonably necessary to enable the Contractor to comply with its obligations under the Main Contract and the CDM Regulations in respect of the health and safety file (as defined in the CDM Regulations),

children.name: text
children: and no extension of time shall be given in respect of the Sub-Contractor's compliance with this Clause 11.4.

children.name: text
children: Without prejudice to any other remedies the Contractor may have the Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor against all claims, liabilities, demands, proceedings, damages, costs, expenses and any fees for intervention imposed on the Contractor by the Health & Safety Executive as a result of any failure by the Sub-Contractor to comply with its obligations under this Clause 11.

children.name: text
children: {b:12. Labour}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall ensure that all labour engaged in connection with the Sub-Contract Works is employed in accordance with the Working Rule Agreement of the National Joint Council for the Building Industry or other Working Rule Agreement applicable to his trade to enable the Contractor to meet its obligations under the said Agreement including those with regard to the recognition of and procedures relating to Trade Unions Trade Union Membership and Representation. The Sub-Contractor shall keep proper records and allow the Contractor to inspect the pay, national insurance and Holidays-with-Pay records of any such labour.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor is committed to improving safety performance and standards in the industry and has aligned their practices with the UK Contractor's Group (UKCG) initiative as described in the UKCG Health and Safety Charter published in June 2009 ("{b:the Charter}"). The Contractor will require that a competent and qualified workforce is employed on all the Contractor's projects in accordance with the Charter.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall ensure that all of its site operatives and/or it's sub-contractors (including any agency labour employed by it) possess and produce to the Contractor prior to such operatives/sub-contractors/ or agency labour commencing work on site, a CSCS card or equivalent documentary evidence from any of the record schemes accepted by the UKCG ("{b:the Relevant Competence Document}").

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor fails to comply with the requirements of Clause 12.3 then the Contractor shall be entitled to require the immediate removal from the site of any such site operatives/sub-contractors or agency labour and the Sub-Contractor shall as soon as possible thereafter, supply replacement site operative(s)/sub-contractor(s)/agency labour who possess and produce to the Contractor the Relevant Competence Documentation. The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor against any and all claims, costs, expenses, losses, damages or liabilities it suffers or incurs as a result of or in connection with the removal from site and replacement of any site operative(s)/sub-contractor(s)/agency labour.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor fails to comply with the requirements of Clause 12.3 then the Contractor shall be entitled to employ the services of an approved assessment centre to determine the competence of any such operatives and obtain the Relevant Competence Documentation. Any costs associated with this process will be borne by the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children: {b:13. Quality Control}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall make himself fully familiar and comply with the requirements of quality control and monitoring under the provisions of the Main Contract insofar as they relate to the Sub-Contract Works as well as the Contractor's own quality control arrangements. The Sub-Contractor shall be deemed to have included in the Sub-Contract Sum for all things including all such competent staff as may be necessary to comply with such requirements and arrangements.

children.name: text
children: {b:14. Assignment and Sub-letting}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall not assign this Sub-Contract nor sub-let any portion thereof without the prior written consent of the Contractor. The Sub-Contractor shall assign to the Contractor the benefit of any and all product guarantees obtained by the Sub-Contractor from its suppliers or sub-contractors in respect of materials and/or equipment incorporated or to be incorporated in the Sub-Contract Works. If so required by the Contractor the Sub-Contractor, to the fullest extent permitted by law, shall assign full right, title and interest in any agreements the Sub-Contractor has entered into with its suppliers or sub-contractors relating to the Sub-Contract Works. If any such agreement entered into by the Sub-Contractor with its suppliers or sub-contractors contains provisions which prevent or restrict the assignment of the benefit of any such agreement to the Contractor then the Sub-Contractor shall procure a collateral warranty from such suppliers and/or sub-contractors in terms required by the Contractor. The Sub-Contractor’s compliance with the terms of this Clause 14 is a condition precedent to the performance by the Contractor of the Contractor’s obligations under this Sub-Contract including the Sub-Contractor's right to receive payment.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor may assign this Sub-Contract without the Sub-Contractor's consent being required.

children.name: text
children: {b:15. Defects and Maintenance}

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall rectify at his own cost any defects, shrinkages or other faults in the Sub-Contract Works due to his failure to properly carry out and complete the Sub-Contract Works in accordance with the Sub-Contract and shall have the like obligations as the Contractor under the Main Contract to rectify any such defects, shrinkages or faults which may arise until the issue of the Certificate of Making Good Defects or any such similar certificate under the Main Contract. A decision by any architect, contract administrator, supervising officer or the like under the Main Contract that works executed by the Sub-Contractor are not in accordance with the Main Contract shall be final and conclusive.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding the provisions of Clause 15.1, the Contractor may notify the Sub-Contractor of any defects that appear in the Sub-Contract Works during the defects liability period of the Works under the Main Contract and the Sub-Contractor shall, at the Sub-Contractor's expense, make good such defects within a reasonable time from notification.

children.name: text
children: {b:16. Determination}

children.name: text
children: 16.1. Should the Sub-Contractor:-

children.name: text
children: abandon or without reasonable cause suspend the carrying out of any part of the Sub-Contract Work; or

children.name: text
children: refuse or fail to remove defective work and/or materials; or

children.name: text
children: fail to comply with Clauses 1.4, 4, 9, 11, 12 or 14 or commit any other material breach of the Sub-Contract and fail to remedy the same after notice in writing from the Contractor;

children.name: text
children: then if such default shall continue for seven days after the date of a written notice specifying the default has been given to the Sub-Contractor by the Contractor or if the Sub-Contractor shall at any time thereafter repeat such default (whether previously remedied or not), the Contractor may without prejudice to any other rights or remedies thereupon by notice by special delivery forthwith determine the Sub-Contractor's employment provided that such notice(s) shall not be given unreasonably or vexatiously.

children.name: text
children: 16.2. The Sub-Contractor's employment under this Sub-Contract shall automatically determine forthwith if it becomes Insolvent. For the purposes of this Clause 16.2, the Sub-Contractor becomes Insolvent:

children.name: text
children: if the Sub-Contractor is a company:

children.name: text
children: when it enters administration within the meaning of Schedule B1 to the Insolvency Act 1986;

children.name: text
children: on the appointment of an administrative receiver or a receiver or manager of its property under Chapter I or Chapter II (as applicable) of Part III of the Insolvency Act 1986;

children.name: text
children: on the passing of a resolution for voluntary winding-up without a declaration of solvency under section 89 of the Insolvency Act 1986; or

children.name: text
children: on the making of a winding-up order under Part IV or V of the Insolvency Act 1986;

children.name: text
children: if the Sub-Contractor is a partnership:

children.name: text
children: on the making of a winding-up order against it under any provision of the Insolvency Act 1986 as applied by an order under section 420 of the Insolvency Act 1986; or

children.name: text
children: when sequestration is awarded on the estate of the partnership under section 12 of the Bankruptcy (Scotland) Act 1985 or the partnership grants a trust deed for its creditors;

children.name: text
children: if the Sub-Contractor who is an individual:

children.name: text
children: on the making of a bankruptcy order against him under part IX of the Insolvency Act 1986; or

children.name: text
children: on the sequestration of his estate under the Bankruptcy (Scotland) Act 1985 or when he grants a trust deed for his creditors;

children.name: text
children: if:

children.name: text
children: he enters into an arrangement, compromise or composition in satisfaction of his debts (excluding a scheme of arrangement as a solvent company for the purposes of amalgamation or reconstruction); or

children.name: text
children: in the case of a Party which is a partnership) each partner is the subject of an individual arrangement or any other event or proceedings referred to in this Clause 16.2, and each of Clauses 16.2.1 to 16.2.4 also includes any analogous arrangement, event or proceedings in any other jurisdiction.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Sub-Contract, if the employment of the Contractor under the Main Contract is determined for any reason then the employment of the Sub-Contractor under the Sub-Contract shall thereupon also automatically determine forthwith.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Clause 16, the Contractor shall be entitled by notice to the Sub-Contractor to determine the Sub-Contractor's employment, under this Sub-Contract or any other contract with the Contractor if, in relation to this Sub-Contract or any other such contract, the Sub-Contractor or any person employed by it or acting on its behalf shall have committed an offence under the Bribery Act 2010 or, where the Employer is a Local Authority, shall have given any fee or reward the receipt of which is an offence under sub-section (2) of section 117 of the Local Government Act 1972.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding any other provision of this clause 16, the Contractor shall be entitled by notice to the Sub-Contractor to immediately determine the Sub-Contractor's employment at any time and for any reason.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor's employment is determined under Clause 16.1, 16.3, 16.3A or16.3B hereof then the following shall apply:

children.name: text
children: the Contractor may expel the Sub-Contractor from the Sub-Contract Works and take over all the materials and plant provided by or on behalf of the Sub-Contractor which are upon the Site or are being used in connection therewith and may use the same to complete the Sub-Contract Works;

children.name: text
children: the Contractor shall be liable only for the value of such part of the Sub-Contract Works properly executed at the date of such determination. Such value shall be calculated in accordance with the Sub-Contract and shall include the value of any unfixed materials and goods for incorporation in the Sub-Contract Works properly stored on the Site and in which property has passed to the Contractor or the Employer but shall include no other sum or sums whatsoever.

children.name: text
children: Where such determination is due to the default of the Sub-Contractor, all damages, costs, losses and expenses incurred by the Contractor in connection with such determination shall be payable by the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor and shall be recoverable as a debt. The Contractor shall have the right to deduct from or set off against any sums due to the Sub-Contractor under this Sub-Contract and/or any other agreement between the Contractor and the Sub-Contractor all such damages, costs, losses and expenses.

children.name: text
children: Subject to clause 8.12, the Sub-Contractor shall not be entitled to payment of any sums that may become due under this Clause 16.4 where the determination is due to the Sub-Contractor's default until completion of the Works and ascertainment by the Contractor of such damages, costs, losses and expenses referred to in Clause 16.4.3.

children.name: text
children: If the Sub-Contractor's employment is determined under Clause 16.2, no further sums under this contract shall become due and/or payable form the Contractor to the Subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: {b:17. Adjudication}

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clause 17.2 if at any time either party is dissatisfied with any matter arising under or in connection with this Sub-Contract the matter may with the agreement of both parties be referred to the representatives of the parties named in the Sub-Contract Particulars ("the {b:Representatives}") who shall meet to resolve the matter. Any agreement reached by the Representatives shall be final, conclusive and binding upon the parties.

children.name: text
children: Any Dispute shall at the request of either party be referred to the adjudication. The party who is referring the dispute to adjudication may make an application for a person to be nominated as the Adjudicator by the President or Vice President for the time being of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.

children.name: text
children: Either party to this Sub-Contract may give notice at any time of his intention to refer a Dispute to adjudication and the Adjudicator to be appointed must be so appointed in accordance with Clause 17.2 within 7 days of the giving of such notice. The adjudication shall be conducted in accordance with the Scheme for Construction Contract 1998.

children.name: text
children: Any such notice of adjudication issued under clause 17.3 shall be accompanied by the referring party's intended referral notice and all documents which are to be included in the referring party's referral notice.

children.name: text
children: {b:18. Litigation / Arbitration}

children.name: text
children: Subject to Clauses 17 and 18.2, the English courts shall have jurisdiction over any Dispute.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding Clause 18.1, if any Dispute relates to any dispute between the Employer and the Contractor under the Main Contract or between the Contractor and any other sub-contractor or supplier arising out of or in connection with the Works then the Contractor may require, an in which case the Sub-Contractor shall be deemed to agree, that such Dispute is referred to the arbitrator appointed or to be appointed to the dispute under the terms of the Main Contract or such other sub-contract (as the case may be) or are resolved by the courts if so required under the terms of the Main Contract, provided always that any reference to arbitration under this Clause 18.2 shall not be opened until after completion or abandonment of the Main Contract Works or termination of the Contractor's employment under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor shall communicate by written notification to the Sub-Contractor which of the courses of action in Clause 18.2 is to be effected and the Sub-Contractor shall take all necessary steps to procure that effect is given thereto. Any award made by an arbitrator to whom such disputes or differences have been referred, shall be final and binding upon the parties hereto and all such proceedings shall, save where such dispute is referred to the courts, be subject to the Arbitration Act 1996.

children.name: text
children: {b:19. Notices and Time Periods}

children.name: text
children: All notices required to be given hereunder by either party shall be in writing (which for the avoidance of doubt shall not include email or other electronic communications) and shall be delivered by hand or by Special Delivery or other pre-paid postal service which requires a signature upon delivery. The notices shall be deemed delivered on the date of receipt if delivered by hand, or the second Business Day after posting if delivered by pre-paid post.

children.name: text
children: Any notice required to be given hereunder by the Sub-Contractor to the Contractor shall be delivered or sent to the Contractor's registered office with a copy thereof at the same time being sent to the Contractor's relevant site or project office. The Sub-Contractor shall provide proof of delivery of any such notice upon request by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: Any notice required to be given hereunder by the Contractor to the Sub-Contractor shall be delivered or sent at the Contractor's option to either the Sub-Contractor's registered office/principal office or to the Sub-Contractor's relevant site or project office.

children.name: text
children: Where under this Sub-Contract an act is required to be done within a specified period of days after or from a specified date the period shall begin immediately after that date. Where the period would include a day, which is a Public Holiday that day shall be excluded.

children.name: text
children: 19.5. If in an emergency, any communication is made orally with respect to health and safety, risk of damage to property or insurance matters, written confirmation of it shall be sent as soon thereafter as is reasonably practicable.

children.name: text
children: {b:20. Proper Law}

children.name: text
children: This Sub-Contract shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Laws of England and Wales.

children.name: text
children: {b:21. Entire Agreement}

children.name: text
children: This Agreement constitutes the whole agreement between the Parties and supersedes any previous arrangement, understanding or agreement between them relating to the subject matter of this Agreement.

children.name: text
children: Each Party acknowledges that, in entering into this Agreement, it does not rely on any statement, representation, assurance or warranty (a "{b:Representation}") of any person (whether a party to this agreement or not) other than as expressly set out in this Agreement. Each Party agrees that the only remedies available to it arising out of or in connection with a Representation shall be for breach of contract as expressly provided in this Agreement.

children.name: text
children: Nothing in this Clause shall limit or exclude any liability for fraud.

children.name: text
children: {b:22. Commencement of Proceedings and Expiry}

children.name: text
children: The Contractor and the Sub-Contractor agree that irrespective of the manner in which this Sub-Contract is executed or made neither party shall rely on any limitation defence that might otherwise be available to it in defence of proceedings commenced less than 12 years after the practical completion of the Works (or, if earlier, less than 12 years after the termination of the Sub-Contractor's employment under this Sub-Contract).

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Sub-Contract, any action under this Sub-Contract in respect of or relating to:

children.name: text
children: any breach or alleged breach of any new build home warranty provided under section 144 of the Building Safety Act 2022;

children.name: text
children: any breach or alleged breach of the duties imposed by Section 1 or Section 2A of the Defective Premises Act 1972 in relation to the Works; and/or

children.name: text
children: any breach or alleged breach of the Contractor's obligation to carry out and complete the Works in compliance with the Building Act 1984 and all relevant subordinate legislation made under that Act,

children.name: text
children: may be brought at any time before the expiration of the period of 15 years from the practical completion of the Works or, in respect of actions referred to in clause 22.2 which relate to rectification works carried out by the Sub-Contractor following practical completion (whether during the defects liability period or thereafter), from the date the relevant rectification works were completed. The Sub-Contractor shall not rely on any limitation defence that might otherwise be available to it in defence of any such action which is commenced before the expiry of the applicable 15-year period. The Sub-Contractor shall continue to maintain professional indemnity insurance covering its liabilities for negligence in respect of any action referred to in this clause 22 in accordance with (and subject to) clause 6 until the expiry of the applicable 15 year period.
